name: Reverse Lunge to High Knee Lift
description: A dynamic single-leg exercise combining a reverse lunge with an explosive drive to bring the rear knee upward at the end of each rep. The knee drive adds a hip flexor and balance challenge and increases the cardiovascular demand compared to a static reverse lunge.

execution.starting_position: Stand tall with feet together, hands on hips or holding light dumbbells at your sides.
execution.setup_instructions: No equipment needed for bodyweight version. If using dumbbells, select a light to moderate load.
steps: Step 1: Step one foot backward into a reverse lunge, lowering the rear knee toward the floor.
Step 2: At the bottom, pause briefly then explosively drive the rear knee upward and forward toward chest height.
Step 3: Balance on the standing leg momentarily at the top with the knee raised high.
Step 4: Return the foot back to the floor and repeat, or alternate legs.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale during the descent. Exhale explosively during the knee drive.
common_mistakes: Using momentum instead of controlled hip flexion for the knee drive
Leaning excessively backward during the knee drive
safety_considerations: Maintain an upright torso throughout to protect the lumbar spine
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full lunge descent (front thigh parallel) followed by full hip flexion on the knee drive.
coaching_cues: Lunge down then drive the knee up high
Balance at the top before stepping back down
